v: in pureness, in knowledge, in perseverance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love,
b: This verse mentions many beautiful qualities, including purity, knowledge, perseverance, kindness, and the Holy Spirit. Today, however, we want to speak especially about sincere love. What is sincere love? It is a genuine, pure love without hypocrisy or selfishness.

There was a young man named Simon who had met with many setbacks and difficulties in life, but he always kept sincere love for others. Every day Simon took the initiative to care for the people around him, whether family, friends, or strangers, and he always did his best to bring them warmth and care.

One day Simon met a homeless man who, in the cold of winter, had no home to go to and not a penny to his name. Many people ignored this homeless man, but Simon reached out a hand. He gave him a warm meal and a warm blanket, and began to talk with him and listen to his story. This small act gave the homeless man hope and comfort and let him feel sincere love.

This story tells us that sincere love can change a person's life. When we treat others with genuine love, we can bring them hope and joy. Such love not only lets others feel God's love, it also makes us channels of God, bringing love to others.

So let us work every day to keep sincere love, whether in the family, at work, or in the community. When we treat others with love, we will be witnesses of the light and will be able to change the world.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you love others with sincere love every day and let God's love flow in your life. Amen!

v: But as you abound in everything—in faith, utterance, knowledge, all earnestness, and in your love to us—see that you also abound in this grace.
b: This passage reminds us that we should act with an abounding heart. We abound in faith, speech, knowledge, and earnestness, and this is an expression of God's rich grace. Yet this passage also tells us that we should abound in love toward others as well.

In a small village there was a young man named John. He was a devout Christian who spread the gospel in the village with his faith and passion. He loved God deeply, always welcomed others, and was willing to help them. Every day he shared the food and resources he had with the poor families of the village, to show God's love.

One day an old woman came to John's door. She was one of the poorest people in the village. She could not afford food and medicine, and her face showed despair and helplessness. John invited her into his home without hesitation and prepared a delicious meal for her to enjoy. He also gave her some money he had saved to help her buy the medicine she needed. By his actions John showed God's love and abundance.

This story tells us that in love toward others, we should abound as John did. When we see the needs of others, we should reach out a hand and care for them in practical ways. This is not only help for others but also an expression of our pursuit of God's pleasure. As the passage says, as we abound in faith, speech, knowledge, and earnestness, we should abound in love toward others too.
Let us treat others with love every day and show God's love through practical action. When our love abounds, we can not only change the lives of others but also bring ourselves more joy and peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you show abounding love every day and care for others through practical action. Amen!

v: that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love. Peace to you, dear family! Welcome to enjoy Soul Snack together. Today God's word says to us: “that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love,
b: In our lives, love is a very important element. It is the foundation of our dealings with people and our connection with God. When we receive Jesus Christ and trust Him to be the Lord of our lives, He will dwell in our hearts and become our foundation. This foundation is firm and can support our faith and allow our love to develop.

Let us imagine a story about a tall skyscraper. The beauty and stability of this building are the result of careful design by architects and engineers. In the same way, when Christ dwells in our hearts, our faith and love can be like a stable building, able to stand the test of wind and rain and become a shelter for others. This foundation gives our love the qualities of firmness and endurance, and whatever difficulties or challenges we face, we can still treat others with love.

One cold winter, an old woman was walking along the street when she saw a homeless man shivering with cold. She decided to take him home and give him warmth and food. This old woman's love was like the foundation of that building, enabling her to care for this person in need. Her love was not merely outward kindness but warmth and care from within. This is because Christ lives in her heart, making her love rooted and grounded.

Dear friends, in this world we need rooted and grounded love to influence others. When we trust in Christ and let Him dwell in our hearts, our love is given greater power and meaning. Such love can change people's lives and let them experience God's immeasurable love. So let us work every day to pass on Christ's love to those around us and become the foundation of their lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your love be rooted and grounded, able to influence and change the lives of others, and remain steadfast in hard times. Amen!

v: This I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and all discernment;
b: The word "love" appears many times in the Bible. It is God's guidance for us and also a virtue we should practice in our dealings with others. The passage tells us that God hopes our love will be rich not only in feeling but will also grow in knowledge and discernment. This means we should keep learning and growing so that we can better understand and apply the principles of love.

A young man went to a village to seek truth and wisdom. He found an elderly sage and asked how he could gain knowledge and discernment. The old sage smiled, took out an empty piggy bank, and said to the young man, "Whenever you learn something new, put it into this jar."

The young man began to learn. He read, observed, and experienced, and each time he learned something new, he put it into the piggy bank. As time passed, the jar grew fuller and fuller, and his knowledge and discernment grew accordingly. He found that this rich knowledge and discernment benefited not only himself but also helped him better understand and show love.

In the same way, we need this on our journey of faith. As we study the Bible and take part in prayer and church life, our spiritual piggy bank will gradually fill up. This knowledge and discernment will guide us in how to show God's love more effectively. We can learn principles about forgiveness, empathy, and serving others, and apply them in our daily lives.

Dear family, let us remember the story of this sage and keep learning and growing, so that our love may abound more and more in knowledge and all discernment. When we do so, we will be better able to understand and apply God's love and bring this love to those around us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your love abound more and more in knowledge and all discernment, and may you become a witness of God's love. Amen!

v: For we have much joy and comfort in your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
b: In this passage we see the apostle Paul's praise and gratitude toward Philemon. Paul felt joy and comfort because Philemon showed abundant love and brought refreshment to the hearts of the saints.
Love is an attitude of devotion, care, and giving. When we treat others with love, we can not only feel joy and comfort ourselves, but also become good news in the hearts of others.

There was a young man who lived in a poor village. Although he did not have many possessions himself, he was always willing to share what he had with others. He often gave his own lunch to those who had no food, and was willing to help the elderly and the disabled with whatever he could do. His love touched the whole village, and the people's care and affection for him were plain to see.

Just as the apostle Paul felt joy and comfort over Philemon, when we bring love to others, we too can experience the same joy and comfort. Our love can change not only the lives of others but also bring satisfaction and peace to our own souls.

So every day, let us treat the people around us with love. Whether with family, friends, coworkers, or strangers, let us meet them with care, patience, and abundant love. When we treat others with love, we can pass on God's love and let others feel a life full of hope, faith, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you not only feel joy and comfort on this journey full of love, but also become good news in the hearts of others. Amen!

v: For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve.
b: This passage reminds us that God is righteous. God will not forget our work, nor the love we have shown for His name. Sometimes we may feel that our efforts have been overlooked, or we feel tired and discouraged. But let us remember that God sees everything, and He will never forget our giving and our love. There was a young man named David, a very zealous Christian who often took part in the church's service. Every week he visited elderly people living alone, cared for poor families, and helped homeless people find shelter. He gave quietly and never expected anything in return.

One day David met a young woman who had suffered a family tragedy. She had lost her family and felt lonely and desperate. David spent a lot of time with her, listened to her heart, and gave her comfort and hope. The young woman gradually recovered her smile and regained courage for life.

A few years later David went through a difficult period. He fell into financial trouble, lost his job, and faced many challenges. He felt helpless and dejected, and even began to doubt his own worth. Yet at his most difficult time, that young woman helped him with everything she had, giving financial support and encouragement. She said, "You were once my savior; now it is my turn to save you."

This story tells us that the work we do and the love we show for God's name are valuable, even at times when they seem ignored or forgotten. God will never forget our giving, and He will repay us when we need it most.

So whatever difficulties or challenges we meet, let us keep serving the saints, loving one another, and passing on love. Like David, we too can become saviors in the lives of others, and find help and encouragement in our own hardest times.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May God give you strength and wisdom to keep serving the saints, loving one another, and passing on love. Amen!

v: who have testified to your love before the assembly. You do well to send them forward on their journey in a way worthy of God,
b: This passage reminds us that our love should not stay only in words but be proved by action. Our love should be real, concrete, and practical. As the passage says, brothers and sisters testified to your love before the church; this is not only your honor but also a response to God.

Everyone longs to be loved and cared for; this is a human need. But sometimes we may only say a light "I love you" and never prove that love in action. True love, however, needs to be shown through action. Just as a child needs the love and company of parents, we also need to support and help one another in each other's lives.

There was a young brother, a veteran who had lost both feet from injuries on the battlefield. His life became full of challenges and difficulties, but he did not give up. Through his unyielding attitude and hard work, he became a successful prosthetics designer.

This brother deeply understood how important the love and help of others had been to him. So he began to take the initiative to help other people with physical disabilities, designing prosthetics better suited to their needs. Through his effort and care, he not only helped many people but also proved his love and his faith in God.

This story tells us that in our daily lives, we too can prove our love through small actions. Perhaps it is only spending a little time with a lonely neighbor, or giving some help to someone in need. These seemingly insignificant actions can bring others faith, hope, and love.

Let us bring this passage and this story into our own lives and think about how we can better prove God's love in daily life. May all our actions be a response to God, drawing us closer to Him and letting others feel God's love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find more growth and fulfillment in the process of proving God's love. Amen!

v: keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life.
b: In our lives, how important it is to keep ourselves in the love of God and look for the mercy of the Lord Jesus. This is the source from which we can find comfort and strength in our most difficult moments. Just as a little bird hides under its mother's wings and is protected and cherished, we too need to place ourselves in God's love and let His mercy surround us.

One day a young girl was walking along the street with tears on her face and despair in her eyes. She had lost the person dearest to her, and her heart was full of pain and helplessness. Just then a friend passed by, saw her, and stopped. He saw the girl's sorrow and held her tightly in his warm embrace. He said, "I know your pain right now, but do not forget that God's love is always here, and He will help you through this difficult time."

This friend was like our Lord Jesus Christ, who always comforts us with love and mercy. When we feel lonely, desperate, and disappointed, we need only look to Him and place ourselves in His arms, and His love will protect us and give us strength.

This passage reminds us not only to keep ourselves in the love of God, but also to look for the mercy of the Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life. When we face challenges and difficulties, let us not lose hope, but believe that the mercy and grace of the Lord Jesus are always with us. Like a little boat on the sea at night looking up to the stars for guidance, let us look to the mercy of the Lord Jesus and let His love be a bright light in our lives.

So let us remind ourselves every day to keep ourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of the Lord Jesus Christ. Whatever we go through, God's love and mercy are eternal, and they will be our strength and guide in life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God's love and mercy be always with you. Amen!

v: But I hold this against you, that you left your first love.
b: In this verse God rebukes His people for leaving their first love. This makes us reflect: have we, too, left our love for God and for people in our faith?

There is a story that tells us about the importance of love. Once, on a bitterly cold winter day, a young man saw a homeless puppy lying in the street, begging in pain for food and warmth. The young man was deeply touched by the puppy's eyes. Braving the cold wind, he took the puppy home and gave it food to eat and a comfortable bed.

But as time passed, the young man gradually forgot the joy and satisfaction the puppy had once brought him. He became busy with work and the trivial matters of life, and gradually grew cold toward the puppy. In the end he coldly decided to send the puppy to a shelter, abandoning it in a cold world.

This story reminds us that just as the young man left his first love for the puppy, we too may leave our first love for God and people in our faith. When we first began to follow Jesus, we were full of love and passion and were willing to give for others. Yet as time passed, we may have been swallowed up by worldly busyness and self-centeredness and forgotten the most important thing: love.

In this world there are too many people in need of love and care: the homeless, the sick, the lonely, and more, who long for true love and care. God calls us to return to our first love, to care for these people in need, and to show the power of love among ourselves.
Let us no longer be cold toward love, but light up this world with love. As the apostle John says in the Bible, “Beloved, let us love one another, for love is of God” (1 John 4:7).
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you return to your first love and care for and cherish those who need love. Amen!

v: The Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all men, even as we also do toward you,
b: Love is a sacred power. It can change our lives and touch the people around us. This passage tells us that God longs for us to love one another, and for our love for everyone to grow and overflow, just as the love given to us has done.

Imagine a beautiful garden filled with all kinds of flowers. Each flower has its own color and fragrance, yet together they create one lovely scene. This is the power of love. When we love one another, we are like those flowers: each person unique and beautiful, yet blended together into one harmonious community.

The power of love is not limited to loving one another; it also moves us to love everyone. There was a young sister who was always ready to lend a helping hand to those around her. She was full of care and thoughtfulness toward everyone, giving her time and energy without expecting anything in return. Her love touched many people, and they began to learn to love others too. Love like this is not a flash that burns out in a moment, but a lasting growth, like a seed that takes root and sprouts in every heart.

Loving everyone is not easy, especially when we meet people who are hard to get along with or who work against us. But if we sincerely seek God’s help, He will plant the seed of love in our hearts and enable us to love even those who are hard to love. As we learn to be patient, to forgive, and to care for others, our love will grow, and we will become more like Jesus Christ.

Let us resolve from today to let love grow in our lives. Whether with family, friends, or everyone we meet, may we be willing to give sincere love and care. When we do, we become witnesses for God, and we can bring others faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you love one another in your daily life and extend that love to those around you. Amen!

v: We are bound to always give thanks to God for you, brothers, even as it is appropriate, because your faith grows exceedingly, and the love of each one of you all toward one another abounds;
b: This passage tells us a story about faith and love. There was a young man who once went through a difficult season and felt hopeless and alone. At that time a Christian friend came to his side and gave him selfless care and love. This friend not only listened to his troubles and worries, but also encouraged him to trust in God’s grace and promises. Such selfless love and the sharing of faith caused the young man’s faith to begin to grow, and he found hope again.

This story reminds us that when we face difficulties and challenges, we need to love and support one another. Our love should abound, like that Christian friend’s. Sometimes a word of encouragement or a sincere smile can change a person’s whole life. When we care for others with love, we not only help them grow and find hope, but we also enrich our own lives.

So let us treat the people around us with love every day, whether family, friends, or even strangers. Let us show Christ’s love through our words and actions and become a blessing in other people’s lives. When we love one another, faith will grow and hope will spring up, and our hearts will be filled with God’s grace and peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you have a heart of abounding love every day and spread that love to those around you. Amen!

v: For whom the Lord loves, he disciplines, and chastises every son whom he receives.
b: In this passage we see that God, as our Heavenly Father, not only loves us but also disciplines us. This discipline does not come from harshness or punishment, but from His love and care for us. Just as loving parents teach their children right values and behavior, God guides us in the same way.

On our life’s journey we may meet many challenges and difficulties. Sometimes these difficulties may be God’s way of disciplining us, helping us grow and keep moving forward. Just as a rough gemstone must be cut and polished before its beautiful brilliance shows, we also need hardship and trials to shape our character and faith.

Think of a young athlete who experienced defeat and setbacks in competition. Yet he did not give up. Instead he worked hard to learn and grow, and in the end he became a successful athlete. In the same way, when we face difficulties, let us not be knocked down by them, but accept them with a positive attitude and learn the lessons in them.

In God’s love we can find courage and hope. Whether we are going through joy or sorrow, God’s love goes with us. Like a mother bird sheltering her chicks, God protects and guides us. Let us believe that whatever we face, God’s plan is good, and He walks beside us.

Let us always remember that God’s discipline comes from His love and care for us. When challenges come, let us meet them with faith and hope, believing that God will lead us through our difficulties to victory. May the truth of this passage take deep root in our hearts and bring us faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s love and blessing every day. Amen!

v: Don’t love the world, neither the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him.
b: In this verse the Lord reminds us not to set our love on the world and its worldly things, because that will draw us away from God’s heart. The things of the world often tempt us and cause us to lose our love and devotion to God. Instead, we should give our hearts and love wholly to God, seeking His will and walking with Him.

In our daily lives there are all kinds of temptations and trials that pull us off God’s path. Think of a climber ascending a high mountain. He meets rugged trails and steep rock faces, but if he keeps firm faith in his goal and overcomes the difficulties, he will finally reach the summit and enjoy the magnificent view.

Or think of a mother who, in the middle of busy housework, still makes time to play with her children. She knows her children are her most important treasure, and she will not spend all her time on cleaning the house or pursuing possessions. She understands that love and care are the foundation of her close relationship with her children.

In the same way, when we love the world and worldly things, we may miss the chance to build a close relationship with God. We should put God first, seek His heart, and show His love and truth in every corner of our lives.

So let us remind ourselves every day not to let the things of the world steal our love for God. Let us not make the pursuit of material things the only goal of our lives, but seek God’s Kingdom and His righteousness.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep this truth in mind at all times and give your love and heart wholly to God. Amen!

v: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
b: In this passage we see that the power of love is strong and irresistible. It goes beyond time, space, and material things. No matter how many difficulties and adversities it faces, love can endure and never be extinguished.

There was a young girl named Tian Li. She was born into a poor family, and her parents could not give her any material comforts. But what they gave Tian Li with all they had was love, warmth, and care. She grew up in hard circumstances, yet she never felt a lack of love. Her parents taught her to value close relationships between people and to cherish one another, even in the hardest times.

When Tian Li grew up, she became a doctor with a heart full of love. She decided to return to her hometown to help those who lacked material things. In her clinic she gave herself selflessly, using her profession to care for everyone who came for help, offering them healing and compassion. She poured her time, energy, and skill into this work, because she deeply believed that love can change a person’s life and bring hope.

This story tells us that even in poverty and hardship, love can light up and transform a life. Just as the Scripture says, many waters cannot quench love, nor can floods drown it. It goes beyond the value of possessions and the exchange of wealth; it is priceless.

May each of us be inspired by this passage to change the world with love. Let us not focus only on our own interests and possessions, but care about the needs of others, giving love and compassion. For only through love can we truly feel God’s blessing and grace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you show the power of love among people and become a messenger who changes the world. Amen!

v: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
b: In this passage Paul teaches us about the matter of food sacrificed to idols. He says that we may understand such things and have some knowledge of them. But we must not stop at knowledge and let it make us proud. Instead, Paul tells us that only love can truly build people up.

Consider a boy named Zhiming. Zhiming was a gifted athlete with outstanding skill and technique. He had unmatched knowledge and knew the rules and techniques of every sport inside out. But his pride overflowed, and he often looked down on others and ignored them because of his achievements and abilities.

One day Zhiming took part in a basketball game. He played brilliantly, but his attitude made people uncomfortable. He mocked, criticized, and found fault with his teammates, which left the whole team tense and discouraged. In the end they lost the game, and Zhiming felt very disappointed.

After that, Zhiming met a coach. The coach told him not to focus only on his own knowledge and skill, but to learn to love. He explained that a team needs everyone’s contribution, and needs cooperation and respect. Only through love could he truly build up the team.

Zhiming thought deeply about this and began to change his attitude. He began to encourage and support his teammates. He learned to cooperate, to use his strengths within the team, and to respect the contributions of others. A few months later, Zhiming’s team entered a basketball tournament again. They showed remarkable unity and fighting spirit, and in the end they won the championship.

This story tells us that knowledge is important, but love is the key to truly building people up. We should learn to respect, cooperate with, and care for one another in daily life. When we treat others with love, we can build more positive relationships and bring others faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you to build up others with love in your life. May God’s grace overflow in your life. Amen!

v: Love is patient and is kind; love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
b: Love is the most beautiful power in this world. It can comfort a wounded soul, light up a dark road, and change people’s lives. But living out such love on our own is not easy; we must humbly rely on the Lord.

In life we often meet many challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we may envy the success of others, or boast and lose our humility. But true love holds no envy or boasting. It can bear with the faults of others and show them kindness and graciousness.

There was a woman named Enhui who ran a small restaurant in her neighborhood. Enhui was very kind and glad to help, and she often gave leftover food to people in need. One day a young girl came into the restaurant. She looked very tired and hungry and could afford only the cheapest food. Enhui was moved with compassion and decided to give the girl a generous meal for free. Enhui did not envy those who had more money than she did; she simply used her own limited resources to help those in need. Love like this is patient and kind.

In the same way, in our own lives we can treat others with love. When we see others succeed, let us not allow envy and boasting to eat away at our souls. Instead, let us be glad for their success and share their joy. Let us treat those who are different from us, or who have weaknesses, with humility and patience, showing them kindness and grace.
Dear family, may we live and act in love every day, so that this world may be filled with the fragrance of faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you grow strong in love and share this love selflessly with those around you. Amen!

v: Love never fails. But whether there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Whether there are various languages, they will cease. Whether there is knowledge, it will be done away with.
b: Prophecies will be done away with, tongues will cease, and knowledge will be done away with.
How important love is in this world! We all need love, whether in receiving it or in giving it. God tells us in the Bible that love is an eternal power that will never cease.

Many things in this world are temporary. The preaching of the prophets will eventually end, the ability to speak in tongues will eventually disappear, and knowledge will fade away. But love will never cease and never fail; it is eternal.

A kind father always loves his child unconditionally. Whatever wrong his son has done, whether he has wandered far away or committed a great sin, the father’s love never changes. Even when his son is at his lowest point, the father’s love stays the same. This is God’s love for us, a love that never ends.

Everyone longs to be loved, and God’s love is exactly what we need. When we feel lonely, disappointed, or worried, God’s love can give us strength and comfort. When we have made mistakes, God’s love declares forgiveness and a new beginning. When we face challenges and difficulties, God’s love can give us courage and hope.

Let us live out this never-ending love every day. Whatever our circumstances, we can respond to others with love, giving them warmth, care, and support. Let us pass on God’s love through our lives, because this is our eternal mission.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s endless love at all times and share that love with others. Amen!

v: If there is therefore any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,
b: In life we often meet difficulties and challenges that leave us discouraged, hopeless, and alone. But in this verse God reminds us that in Christ we can receive every kind of spiritual abundance.

Love is one of them. Love is a source of warmth and comfort, and when we are in trouble it can give us strength and hope. It is like a winter morning when we are curled up in the cold and someone hands us a cup of hot tea that warms us body and soul, and we feel the tenderness of love.

In this world love is very important. When we show concern and love to others, we not only help them through hard times, but also bring ourselves joy and satisfaction. Just as the sun shines on all the flowers, our love can light up other people’s lives and let them feel God’s love.

The Holy Spirit is our Helper and Guide. When we draw near to the Holy Spirit and have fellowship with Him, He gives us wisdom and strength to face the challenges of life. Just as a compass guides a ship at sea, the Holy Spirit can lead us on the right path, however fierce the storm.

Tender mercies and compassion in our hearts are our concern and care for others. When we share in their joys and sorrows, we show our love for them and also reveal God’s lovingkindness. Like a mother with her child, our compassion can give others strength and encouragement and let them feel God’s mercy.

Dear family, may you find exhortation in Christ, love, fellowship of the Spirit, and tender mercies and compassion in your hearts. In every difficulty, do not lose faith and hope, for God is with us and gives us everything we need.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience the comfort of God’s love in the midst of life’s storms, and may you feel the guidance of the Holy Spirit in every trial. Amen!

v: make my joy complete, by being of the same mind, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind.
b: In this passage Paul reminds us to treat one another with the same love and the same mind. He tells us that doing so not only gives him joy, but, more importantly, such unity and harmony deeply affects the life of each one of us.

We live today in a world full of division and strife, and it is easy to be affected by negative outside influences. Yet God calls us to have the same mind and the same thoughts. What does this mean? It means we choose to look at others with love and acceptance. No matter who they are, and no matter how they differ from us in faith, values, or opinions, we should hold love toward them.

A young man joined a summer camp where he lived and studied with people from all over the world. At the camp he met a friend from a different culture and religious background. At first, because of their differences, there were some misunderstandings and disagreements between them. But through honest communication and mutual respect, they gradually discovered what they had in common and the worth in each other. In the end they became the best of friends and had a deep influence on each other’s lives.

This story tells us that when we are willing to understand and accept others, we find connection and harmony between us. The same love and the same mind enable us to rise above disagreement and conflict and build true friendship and relationship.

So let us work, in our daily lives, to understand and embrace others and to treat them with the same love. This will not only bring joy and peace to us and to others, but, more importantly, this attitude will show the love and truth of Christ.

On this beautiful morning, let us pray together to God, asking Him to give us the same love and the same mind. May we encourage and support one another and bring faith, hope, and love to those around us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you love one another in your daily life and treat others with the same love and mind. Amen!

v: that their hearts may be comforted, they being knit together in love, and gaining all riches of the full assurance of understanding, that they may know the mystery of God, both of the Father and of Christ,
b: Brothers and sisters, let us reflect together on the truth of this passage. It reminds us that we must be knit together in love in order to find comfort and rich faith on the path of believing. I would like to share a moving story with you to inspire us in how to live out this love.

Once there was a little boy named Guohua, who was always bullied by his classmates at school. Every day when he got home he was silent, his eyes full of pain and helplessness. One day a classmate named Zhigang saw this and decided to step forward and show concern for him.

Zhigang began chatting with Guohua and listened as he poured out the pain in his heart. Zhigang did not only listen; he also gave Guohua encouragement and support. He told Guohua, “You are not alone. I will always be by your side to look after you.” This love was like a warm hand gently touching Guohua’s soul. From then on Guohua gradually grew stronger. He knew someone cared for him, and he began to face each day with confidence.

This story tells us that in life we can help others through love and empathy. Each of us has the ability to be a Zhigang in someone else’s life, giving care and support. When we care for others with sincere love, we can not only change their lives, but also enrich our own faith.

Just as the Scripture says, when we are knit together in love, our hearts are comforted and our faith becomes rich. We can support one another, grow together on life’s journey, and explore the mystery of God together. When we have this kind of faith, we can know Christ more deeply and obey His will more fully.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find comfort as you are knit together in love, may your faith be full, and may you truly know the mystery of God, which is Christ. Amen!

v: Blessed is the man who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to those who love him.
b: Based on this verse, let us think together about the blessings and challenges of those who love God. Life is full of temptations and difficulties, but when we take love for God as our guide and motivation, we will receive rich blessings.

Imagine a man who faced one setback and difficulty after another and even doubted God’s existence and care. Yet he did not give up. He chose to love God and trust His plan. During that time he learned endurance and perseverance, and he came to see that temptations and difficulties were no longer things that destroyed him, but opportunities to grow and be shaped.

This man’s story tells us that when we love God, we are given strength to face the challenges of life. We will not be trapped in our difficulties, but will grow stronger through every trial. Just as gold must be refined by fire to shine with its beautiful brilliance, we also must go through testing to show our true worth and faith.

This steadfast love and faith also let us see that trials are not only suffering and pain, but precious opportunities God gives us. When we walk with God and persevere and endure through trials, we begin to understand His plan and purpose. We begin to grasp the value of the crown of life, a treasure that surpasses worldly riches, the wonderful blessing of being with the Lord.

Dear family, whatever hardship you are in now, let us remember God’s promise. When we love God and trust His love and guidance, we will receive the crown of life as our reward. This is not only hope for the future, but also comfort and strength for today.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you show a steadfast love for God and faith when you face testing and difficulty. May you experience God’s blessing and growth, and become a person who loves God, bringing more faith, hope, and love to the world. Amen!

v: Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently:
b: This passage reminds us that once we have received God’s truth and let His word cleanse our hearts, we should love our brothers and sisters with sincere love. This love is without hypocrisy. It flows from deep within us and truly affects our relationships with others.

In our daily lives we often have opportunities to show this unfeigned love. We can encourage, support, and help those in need. Think of a mother caring for her child, pouring out all her love and care without counting the cost or expecting anything back. This example of a mother’s love tells us that sincere love asks for nothing in return, but cares for others with zeal and a selfless heart.

We can also find more insight in the life of Jesus. Jesus paid an enormous price with His own body for our sins, the greatest expression of love. Jesus’ love is unconditional and asks nothing in return. Even when we make mistakes and turn away from Him, He is always willing to forgive us and receive us with love.

Let us follow the example of Jesus’ love and love one another without hypocrisy in our daily lives. Whether at home, in church, or at work, let us treat others with sincere hearts and give them care and support. Such love can not only bring others hope and courage, but also change our own lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience sincere love every day and pass that love on to others. Amen!

v: But whoever has the world’s goods, and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart of compassion against him, how does the love of God remain in him?
b: This passage reminds us of our responsibility as Christians: not only devotion in faith, but passing on our love and care to those in need. When we have abundant possessions, are we willing to share that abundance with others?
There was a young businessman who was very successful and had great wealth. But his heart gradually grew cold and selfish. Busy each day making money, he overlooked the many poor people around him.

One day he met an old woman begging on the street. He was deeply moved by her sad condition and decided to help her. He bought her food and clothing and even provided a warm house for her to live in. As time went by, he gradually regained his joy and found that the love in his heart had been rekindled.

This businessman realized that true wealth is not only material but of the heart. He began to reach out to the people around him and was willing to share his wealth and love. He founded a charitable organization to help those in need. His life became full of meaning and satisfaction.

This story tells us that when we have wealth, we need the courage to share it with those in need. We must keep hearts of compassion and care, so that the love of God may remain in us. Only then can we truly experience God’s blessing and bring others faith, hope, and love.
Let us pray together to our Heavenly Father, asking Him to give us loving hearts so that we may extend this love to those in need.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive abundant joy and peace as you share love. Amen!

v: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.
b: This passage reminds us that fear cannot exist in God’s love. When we live in love, fear vanishes without a trace. The nature of fear is dread of punishment, but in God’s love we have been made complete.

In our daily lives many things can stir up fear in us: perhaps uncertainty about the future, pressure at work, or difficulties in relationships. Yet when we embrace God’s love and believe His promises, fear can no longer occupy our souls. There was a man named Derek who had always dreamed of becoming an outstanding musician. But because of an embarrassing experience on stage as a child, he was extremely afraid of sharing his music with others. He feared being laughed at, being rejected, and the possibility of failure.

But Derek decided to overcome this fear. He began to invest time and effort in learning how to overcome fear and used love to motivate himself. He often recalled God’s love for him and believed that God would protect him in his efforts. In the end Derek overcame his fear and became an excellent musician, bringing joy and encouragement to many people in the world of music.

This story tells us that as long as we walk in love, fear cannot stop us from achieving our dreams and goals. On our journey of faith there may be many challenges and difficulties, but we can lay down our fear and trust in God’s love and protection.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that Your love is always with us. Help us overcome fear, and let us live out a steadfast faith, hope, and love in Your love. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you walk through each day in faith and deeply experience God’s love. Amen!

t: Not Loving the Brother You Have Seen
v: If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?
b: This passage reminds us that love is an indispensable element of the Christian life. The God we believe in is the source of love, and He asks us to treat one another with love.

In life we meet all kinds of people. Some are easy for us to love because they share our values and interests. But others may be hard for us to love because their words, actions, or backgrounds make us uncomfortable.
Yet the Scripture tells us that we cannot love only the people who are easy to love; we need to learn to love everyone God has made. Consider the story a Christian brother once shared:

One time he met a beggar on the street, a man in ragged clothes with no home to go to. Instinctively he felt a flicker of disgust, but he immediately realized that this was also a person God loves. He walked over, chatted with the man, and listened to his story. The beggar told him he had once been a successful businessman, but after a series of disasters he had lost everything. The brother was deeply moved by the story and felt that God was leading him to love this man whom society had cast aside.

This story helps us understand that love has no conditions. No matter who a person is, and no matter their background, they deserve to be treated with love. When we love a person, we are showing God’s love to the world.

So let us ask ourselves every day: Did I show love to the people around me today? For those who need love, are we willing to sacrifice our time and energy to care for them? Let us not only say that we love God, but love His creation in practical action.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you treat others with love every day and experience God’s love in doing so. Amen!

v: May the God of peace himself sanctify you completely. May your whole spirit, soul, and body be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
b: In this passage we see that God wants to give us a life of peace, sanctification, preservation, and being blameless. This is His blessing and promise to us. But have we truly experienced such a life?
There was a young man who, under the pressure of work and life, felt exhausted and anxious. He was always under stress and felt no calm or rest. Then one day he met a wise man.

The wise man told the young man a parable. He said there was a bird that he wanted to stop flitting about, so he tried to find it a quiet place. He gave the bird a cage, and after he put the bird inside, it began to torment itself, beating against the cage and trying to escape. The wise man told the young man that only when the bird stopped struggling could it find calm and rest in the cage.

In the same way, we need to stop and no longer chase after worldly busyness and anxiety. We can trust in God, entrust ourselves fully to Him, and seek inner peace. This is not only peace of body and mind, but spiritual peace. When we pursue sanctification and keep our spirit, soul, and body preserved, we can be found blameless at the coming of Jesus Christ.

When we live out this kind of peace and sanctified life, we will also become a witness to others. The peace and joy in us will touch those around us and make them long to seek a relationship with God. Let us show this peace through our lives and conduct and become a blessing in other people’s lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience the peace God gives in faith, hope, and love. May your spirit, soul, and body be preserved, and may you be blameless at the coming of Jesus Christ! Amen!

v: The God of peace will bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
b: This passage reminds us that we have a God of peace, who will crush Satan under our feet so that we can have true peace. Peace is what we long for in this noisy world. We are often troubled by pressure, worry, and fear, but God says to us that He gives us peace and will crush the power of Satan under our feet.

A traveler was walking along a steep and dangerous mountain path. He had lost his way, and his heart was full of fear and unease. Suddenly he saw a compass pointing in one direction and showing him the right road. That compass represents the peace God gives us. It guides us onto the right path and away from fear and unease.

In life we may also meet storms and difficulties, but we can trust God’s promise: He will crush Satan under our feet, He will protect us, and we can find peace in the midst of trouble. Like a captain guiding his ship through raging waves, God will also lead us through hardship and give us peace.
Let us treasure the peace God gives us, entrust our worries and fears to Him, and believe His promise, for He is our true protector and the giver of peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive God’s peace in every difficulty, and may His grace be with you! Amen!

v: The things which you learned, received, heard, and saw in me, do these things, and the God of peace will be with you.
b: In this passage Paul reminds us that it is not enough merely to hear and receive the teaching; what matters more is to live it out. If we only listen and do not put it into practice, then these lessons and this knowledge will stay in our heads and cannot truly bring change.

Imagine a gardener who, over many years of study and observation, has understood how plants grow and the skills of gardening. He patiently learns how to plant, fertilize, and prune, but this knowledge works only when he actually puts his hands to the planting. In the same way, we as Christians need to take action and apply in our lives the truth we have learned, heard, and seen.

Perhaps when you are in trouble you feel helpless and despairing. At such times we can recall the stories of the Bible, such as Elijah on Mount Carmel facing the four hundred fifty prophets of Baal. He was not discouraged; he prayed to God and finally witnessed God’s great power and lovingkindness. This story reminds us that even in the darkest hour, as long as we keep firm faith and rely on God, He will surely be with us and give us peace.

When we put God’s word into practice in our lives, we can also become God’s witnesses, bringing hope and courage to others. Think of how Jesus, in the Gospel of Matthew, called His disciples and sent them out to proclaim the Kingdom of God. The disciples not only heard Jesus’ teaching; they also saw with their own eyes God’s miracles and power, and then carried the good news to the whole world. Their actions changed not only their own lives, but the whole world.

So, dear family, let us not only hear the word but also do it. In our daily lives, let us weave God’s word into our words and conduct and become God’s witnesses. Believe God’s promise of peace: whatever stage of life we are in, He is with us, giving us strength and courage to face every difficulty and challenge.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you often experience God’s peace and blessing as you walk along the way. Amen!

v: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
b: In this verse we see God’s plans and intentions for us. God does not intend to bring disaster upon us. On the contrary, His thoughts toward us are to give us peace, to bless us, and to give us hope in the end.

Difficulties and challenges are inevitable in our lives, but this does not mean God has abandoned us. On the contrary, through this verse God tells us that His plan is to give us peace and hope. Like parents with their children, God cares about our every step, and He wants us to have a good future.

In our lives we sometimes face setbacks and disappointments, perhaps a failure at work or a broken relationship. But when we feel despair, let us hold on to the truth of this verse. God’s plan and intention is to give us peace, so that even in hardship we can keep our faith and look forward to the hope of the future.

There was a young man named Peter who had dreamed since childhood of becoming a musician. But in an important competition Peter made a mistake, and he felt deeply despairing and disappointed. Peter thought his road in music had come to an end, and he even considered giving up music.

But just when he felt hopeless, he met a teacher. The teacher told him that a mistake does not mean failure; it is a chance to learn and grow. He encouraged Peter to believe in his talent, to persevere, and to seek improvement.

Peter listened to his teacher, pulled himself together, and worked hard at study and practice. In the end he entered the competition again and achieved astonishing results, winning everyone’s praise and admiration.

This story tells us that even in failure and setbacks we can still look forward to a hopeful future. God gives us thoughts of peace so that we can keep going and believe in our own abilities and potential.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. When you face difficulties, do not give up, but believe that God gives us thoughts of peace. May you keep your faith in every challenge. Amen!

v: “My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him that he might be reverent toward me; and he was reverent toward me, and stood in awe of my name.
b: In this verse God tells us that He has made a covenant of life and peace with us. This covenant gives us a heart that reveres God and leads us to reverence and awe because of His name. This is God’s grace and promise to us, and it is also the foundation of our lives as Christians.

Life and peace are gifts everyone longs to have, but sometimes in life we do not feel true peace. Perhaps it is because of troubles and pressure, perhaps because of the loss of a loved one, or perhaps because of unstable circumstances. Yet God’s word reminds us that He has already given us a covenant of life and peace. This means that whatever difficulty or adversity we are in, we can look to Him and seek His peace.

There was once a young man named Mark who went through a series of setbacks and failures in life. He lost his job and felt helpless and despairing. But in his darkest hour he decided to turn to God and seek His peace.

One day Mark saw a little bird in a park. The bird looked very happy, flying freely in the sky. Mark thought that perhaps the little bird knew some secret that he did not. So he began to watch the bird, and he found that it had no worry or fear, and no sense of lack. It simply trusted its own wings and the God who feeds it.

This story tells us that, like the little bird, we too should trust God, believe His promises, and live out the life and peace He has given us. When we hand our worries and fears over to Him and rest in the assurance that He will care for us, His peace will fill our hearts.

So we can live out this truth in our daily lives. When we face challenges and difficulties, let us not be afraid, but seek God’s peace and wisdom. Let us believe His promises, pursue a heart that reveres God, and live out the life and peace He has given us. Living this way will not only bring calm to our hearts, but also spread God’s love and hope around us.
pr: We ask that God give us the strength to revere Him, trust in Him, and live out the life and peace He has given us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel His love and healing every day. Amen!

v: Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them; and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them forevermore.
b: This passage tells us that God has bound Himself to us with a covenant of peace, and that He will set us in His grace and cause our numbers to keep growing. At the same time, God will build His sanctuary in our lives and be with us forever.

One man went through many setbacks and difficulties and felt he had lost faith and hope. He felt he was in darkness, lost and confused. But he held on to his faith and prayed to God every day. One day he heard the words of this passage and was deeply moved. He began to believe that God has a plan and a purpose, and that his life was no accident.

This man decided to rebuild his relationship with God and receive the covenant of peace God has made. He entrusted himself fully to God, believing that God would lead him out of his troubles. Before long he began to see change. His outlook gradually shifted, and hope and joy filled his heart. He began to meet many people who helped him, and he welcomed new opportunities. God began to build a sanctuary in his life and became the center of his living.

This story tells us that whatever situation we are in, if we are willing to receive God’s covenant of peace and trust His leading, He will surely lead us toward a bright future. Like the man in the story, we also need to keep in continual contact with God, entrust ourselves fully to Him, and believe that He has a good plan and purpose.

Let us face the challenges of life every day with faith, hope, and love. However hard the times we meet, remember that God has made an everlasting covenant of peace with us, and He will lead us toward success and victory.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true peace and joy in receiving God’s covenant of peace, and may you keep growing in His grace. Amen!

t: A Covenant of Peace That Will Not Be Removed
v: For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed; but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,” says Yahweh who has mercy on you.
b: In this passage God assures us that His lovingkindness and peace will never leave us. Great mountains and small hills may be moved, but God’s love and peace are firm and unshakable.

A preacher once shared an inspiring story about a young woman named Yuru. Her life had been full of hardship and setbacks. She came from a poor family, could not receive a good education, and faced all kinds of challenges. Yet she never gave up hope and faith.

Yuru decided to use the resources and abilities she had to work to change her destiny. She worked and studied hard, and went through many difficulties on this arduous journey. But she never forgot God’s promise to her, that His love and peace would never leave her. This became the strength and guide that kept her going.

In the end Yuru overcame the many difficulties and became a successful professional. Her story encourages us that whatever challenges we face, as long as we hold fast to faith, hope, and love, God’s lovingkindness and peace will always be with us.

This passage and Yuru’s story remind us that on the journey of life we may meet high mountains and low valleys, but God’s love and peace do not change. Whatever difficulty we face, as long as we believe God’s promise and hold to His way, we can overcome every hardship.
So let us not be crushed by difficulties, but firmly believe God’s promise, and use our resources and abilities to pursue success. Whatever road we travel, God’s love and peace will be with us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. At every step of your journey, may God’s love and peace continue to keep you and give you strength and courage. Amen!

v: Blessed be Yahweh, who has given rest to his people Israel, according to all that he promised. There has not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by Moses his servant.
b: Looking at this passage, we can deeply sense God’s love and faithfulness to us. God’s promises do not remain only in words; they are truly fulfilled in our lives.
Perhaps you have gone through hardship and setbacks and felt you had lost your direction and hope. But when we trust God and hold to His word, God’s peace will come into our hearts.
In a small town there lived an old grandmother named Mary. She had met with much difficulty and suffering in her life, yet she always kept a heart of peace and joy.
One day a young man asked her, “Grandma, why are you always so calm and happy? Your life doesn’t look easy.”

Mary smiled and answered, “Child, it is because I believe God’s promises. He promised to bless us and to let us find peace in hard times.” She went on, “No matter how many storms and challenges we face, God’s peace is always there.”

This story tells us that God’s peace is not affected by outward circumstances, but comes from our relationship with God. When we lay down all our troubles and worries and entrust everything to God, His peace will fill our hearts.

So whatever difficulty or challenge you face now, remember God’s promise. He gives us peace, a peace that surpasses all human understanding. As long as we believe His word and rely on His strength, we can find peace and hope in hardship.
Let us entrust ourselves to God every day, believe His promises, and, led by faith, hope, and love, live a life full of peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel the peace God gives you at all times, and may your heart be filled with faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: Yahweh, you will ordain peace for us, for you have also done all our work for us.
b: When we face the challenges and difficulties of life, we often feel discouraged and disappointed. We may wonder whether we can find true peace. This verse assures us that when we rely on God, He will surely ordain peace for us.

A young girl named Shiting had gone through many misfortunes in her life, but she always held on to her belief in God’s promises. One day Shiting found a Bible full of verses about peace and hope. Every morning she memorized these verses by heart and began to put them into practice in her life.

Once Shiting met a classmate at school who was very hard to get along with and often hurt her feelings. But Shiting chose to forgive her and responded with friendship and gentleness. The classmate was influenced by Shiting and began to change her behavior.

At another time Shiting’s family ran into financial difficulties and faced a shortage of money. Even so, her family always believed that God would provide for their needs. They kept praying and waited in faith for God’s help. In the end an unexpected opportunity came, and they received an unexpected sponsorship that solved their financial problems.

These stories and our passage all tell us that when we put our faith in God, He will surely ordain peace for us. Whatever difficulty we face, God will give us strength and wisdom to deal with it and will lead us to victory.

So let us hold on to our faith and believe God’s promises. Do not be overwhelmed by difficulty and disappointment, for God has already ordained peace for us. All that we do in life, God gives us the success of it. As long as we rely on Him, He will surely set us on the right path and give us true peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s peace and strength in all things. Amen!

v: I form the light, and create darkness. I make peace, and create calamity. I am Yahweh, who does all these things.
b: In this passage God reveals His sovereignty and power to us. He is the Creator, who can create light and darkness, and who can give peace and send calamity. This reminds us that everything we face is in His hands.

In life we often meet challenges and trials, and sometimes we even feel confused and hopeless. But let us not forget that God can bring us peace through adversity. Like a rainbow after the rain, God’s peace always appears in our hardest moments.

A child once got lost in the forest. He searched everywhere but could not find the way home. He was frightened and despairing, and tears were about to fall. Just then a little bird flew onto his shoulder, as if telling him not to be afraid. After the child had followed the bird for a while, he saw a beam of sunlight shining down through a gap in the trees. He knew this was the way home, and so he found his direction.

This story tells us that just as the little bird led the child out of his trouble, God will also guide us to the path of peace. When we feel helpless and confused, we can seek His help and believe that He will lead us toward peace and toward a way to solve our problems.

So let us not be afraid to face hardship and challenge, because God is the Creator, and He has the authority and power to give us peace. When we are in adversity, let us always remember His promise and guidance, believing that He will give peace when we need it most.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s peace in every difficulty and challenge. When you cannot find a way out, may you seek His guidance and believe that He will show you the way forward. May your heart be filled with faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
b: In life we often face all kinds of challenges and difficulties that leave us under pressure and worried. Sometimes we may feel we cannot cope with these troubles and have lost our peace. But through this verse God calls us to believe that He is a Lord who is willing to give us peace in person.

Imagine a person lost in a storm, wandering and not knowing what to do. He is afraid and alone and does not know where to go for shelter. Just then a kind stranger comes up, reaches out a hand, leads him out of the danger, and brings him to a warm and peaceful place.

God is that kind stranger. When we are lost in life, afraid, and alone, God is willing to give us peace in person. He knows what we need, and He is willing to guide us out of our troubles and lead us into His embrace. Just as the stranger led the lost man to a place of shelter, God is also willing to lead us to a refuge of peace.

There was once a young man named Alexander who faced many difficulties and pressures in his career and felt very discouraged and hopeless. He did not know how to deal with these challenges and felt he had lost his peace. Then one day he met a teacher, who told him a story.

In the story, a boatman was rowing on a lake when suddenly a fierce wind rose and the waves surged high. The boatman was terrified, but he entrusted his fate to God and prayed for peace. At that very moment God calmed the wind and the waves, and the lake became still. The boatman was astonished and grateful, and he knew this was peace God had given him in person.

This story helped Alexander realize that he only needed to hand his troubles over to God and pray for peace, and God would give him peace in person. So Alexander began, every morning when he got up, to place everything before God and pray for peace. He found that when he trusted God and entrusted everything to Him, the power of the peace God gave him was beyond what he had imagined.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. In every challenge and difficulty, may you believe that God is a Lord who is willing to give you peace in person. He knows your needs, and He is willing to guide and protect you. Just as the boatman prayed for peace in the storm on the lake and God calmed the wind and the waves, so when you hand the troubles of your life over to God and ask for His peace, God will give you peace in person. Trust Him and rely on Him, and in every challenge you will find a refuge of peace. Amen!

v: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, do I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
b: This passage reminds us that the Lord Jesus has left us a precious gift: peace. This peace is not the surface calm and comfort the world gives, but a peace deep within the heart, a peace that can be kept no matter what the outward circumstances are.

There was a young girl named Lia who lived in a poor family, where financial pressure and family quarrels always left her troubled and fearful. Yet every morning Lia found a quiet corner to read the Bible and seek the Lord’s peace. Though she was in hardship, her faith never wavered, because she knew the Lord Jesus had given her a peace that surpasses understanding.

Once in Lia’s life she met an old woman who looked deeply troubled. Lia went up to her and asked if she needed help. The old woman told her that she had lost her husband, and that financial difficulty and health problems at home left her utterly distressed. Lia comforted her, saying that we can trust the promise of the Lord Jesus. He has given us peace, and in any kind of hardship we can find comfort and hope through the Lord’s love and power.

This story reminds us that in life we often meet difficulty and challenge, but we must not be troubled or fearful. For the Lord Jesus has opened for us a door that leads to peace. When we lose our way, He is our compass; when we are worn out, He is our strength; when we feel alone, He gives us His constant company.
Dear family, may the peace of the Lord Jesus fill your heart, and may we walk into the future each day under His keeping.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience peace and hope in all things. Amen!

v: Yahweh will give strength to his people. Yahweh will bless his people with peace.
b: In this passage God assures us that He will give us strength and the blessing of peace. What encouraging news this is! When we face challenges, hardship, or uncertain times, we can trust in God’s strength and peace to help us through.

In our lives we often meet storms and tests. Sometimes we may feel powerless, helpless, and confused. But when we seek God’s strength, He gives us strength beyond what we imagine to overcome our difficulties. When David faced the giant Goliath, he did not rely on his own strength but trusted in God’s power. With God’s help he defeated Goliath and became a hero of Israel.

In the same way, when we face difficulties and challenges, we can rely on God’s strength to overcome. He gives us courage and wisdom so that we can face any difficulty. A doctor treating a patient must use professional knowledge and skill; likewise, we need to use the strength and wisdom God gives us to meet the challenges of life.

In addition, God promises to bless us with peace. This peace does not mean only outward calm, but inner stillness and comfort. Wherever we are and whatever we face, God’s peace, which surpasses our understanding, can guard our hearts. Think of sailors in a storm: if they can stay calm and keep their faith, they can steady the ship and bring everyone safely through dangerous waters.

So let us come before God anew each day and seek His strength and peace. When difficulties come, do not be afraid, for God will surely give us the strength we need. When we feel discouraged or anxious, let us turn to God and ask for His peace to soothe our souls.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s strength and peace in your life. Amen!

v: for they will add to you length of days, years of life, and peace.
b: In this passage we see God’s promise to add peace to us. Peace is what we long for in this restless world. When we face difficulties and pressure, peace is a precious treasure, giving us inner calm and stability.

There was a young girl named Xinping. Every day she had to face troubles at home and poverty, yet she had a heart full of faith, hope, and love. Whenever she felt discouraged, she would look up at the sky and tell herself, “God will protect me and give me peace.”

Through her firm faith and her reliance on God, Xinping overcame many difficulties. She believed that God would walk beside her and care for all her needs. In the end she not only got through those hard days, but also gained peace and blessing in her life.

This story reminds us that even in hardship we can have peace. When we place our faith in God and believe His promise, He will give us the peace we need. However great the difficulty we face, God’s peace will guard our hearts and give us strength and courage to face everything.

So let us ask God for peace every day. When we feel uneasy and afraid, let us be convinced that God is our protector and that He will add peace to us. Wherever we are and whatever we go through, God’s peace will lead us out of trouble and bring us hope and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive God’s peace and blessing every day. Amen!

t: Peace to Everyone Who Does Good
v: but glory and honor and peace to every man who works good, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
b: This passage tells us that when we do good, God will give us glory, honor, and peace. This is a message full of hope and encouragement, letting us know that if we persist in doing good, God will surely bless us.

I would like to use an illustration from daily life to inspire us. Imagine the story of a farmer. This farmer worked hard on his fields, planted delicious fruits and vegetables, and shared his harvest with his neighbors. Because of his hard work and generosity, he not only gained a rich harvest but also won the respect and praise of his community. His farm was filled with peace and joy, because he knew his labor was blessed by God.

This story tells us that, like the farmer, when we work hard to do good and share our love and kindness with others, God will give us peace and honor. This does not refer only to material abundance, but, more importantly, to inner peace and joy. When we treat others with love and help them, God pours His grace and peace into our lives.

Let us remember this truth in our daily lives. Whatever difficulty or challenge we meet, as long as we keep doing good, God will surely add peace and honor to us. So let us face everyone with kindness and love, and believe in God’s grace and promise, for He is our true protector and provider.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive peace, honor, and God’s grace on the road of doing good. Amen!

t: Peace to the Far and the Near
v: I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near,” says Yahweh; “and I will heal him.”
b: In this passage God reveals to us His hope and love for us. He is not only willing to give us peace, but also willing to heal our wounds. This is a message full of faith, hope, and love, so let us explore this truth.

In life we often face all kinds of challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we may feel far from God, as if He were at the ends of the earth. We may feel isolated and helpless, with no one to rely on. But this passage tells us that God’s peace and well-being can be given even to those who are far from Him. Wherever we are, God’s love and care will reach us.

Moreover, God is also willing to heal our wounds. Life often brings much pain and trauma that leave us weary and helpless. But this passage reminds us that God cares not only for our physical health but also for the health of our souls. He is our Healer, and He is willing to heal the wounds and pain of our hearts.

A young man met with a great setback: he lost his job, and the support of his family and friends. He felt utterly despairing and alone, as if the world had closed a door on him. Yet in his darkest hour he heard the words of a kind person: “God’s peace and well-being are given to you, and He is willing to heal your wounds.” These words touched him deeply and restored his faith and hope.

This story tells us that even in our hardest times, God’s love and care do not go far from us. His peace and well-being can be given to every person, wherever we are and whatever difficulty we have gone through. He is our Healer, and He is willing to heal the wounds and trauma of our hearts.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. In every difficulty, may you feel God’s peace and well-being. May He heal your wounds and give you faith and hope. Amen!

v: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
b: In this passage we see God’s blessing for us, which is grace and peace. Grace is the gift and love God gives us without condition, and peace is feeling God’s comfort and protection in life.

A young child named Mingde met with many difficulties and pressures at school. He always felt insecure and afraid to face challenges. One day he met a loving teacher, who told him, “Mingde, God has given you grace. You are one of a kind, and you have unlimited potential. If you believe in yourself and work hard, you will overcome every difficulty.”

Mingde was deeply moved by these words. He began to believe in himself and no longer feared challenges. He studied hard and persevered, and in the end he achieved excellent grades. Not only that, he became a model student at his school and led other classmates onto the road to success.

As this story shows, each of us has been given grace and potential by God. We have unlimited possibilities, and if we believe in ourselves and face difficulties bravely, we can overcome everything. God’s grace makes us strong and brave in pursuing our dreams, and whatever difficulties we meet, we can safely rely on God’s strength and guidance.

So let us remind ourselves every day that God gives us grace and peace, and we can face the challenges of life with confidence. Whatever difficulties we meet, let us keep God’s word in mind, believe in our own worth and ability, and rely on God’s strength to face them.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. In every challenge, may you feel God’s grace and peace and experience His strength and guidance. Amen!

v: The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former,” says Yahweh of Armies; “and in this place will I give peace,” says Yahweh of Armies.
b: This passage tells us that God will give us, in this world, a glory greater than before, and will give us peace. When we walk with God, He accomplishes greater things, and we can enjoy the peace He gives.

A little girl named Lina dreamed of becoming a painter. Every day she buried herself in her work, showing her passion and talent. But her family and friends often doubted her dream and thought she would not succeed. Lina felt discouraged, but she held on to the conviction in her heart and believed she had the ability to bring people beauty and joy through painting.

She entered an art competition, but when the results were announced she did not win any prize. Lina felt disheartened and began to wonder whether her ability and her dream were worth holding on to. Yet at that very moment of loss, a miracle happened.

An artist saw Lina’s work and was drawn to her painting skill and subject matter. The artist decided to hold a solo exhibition to show Lina’s work and display her talent. The exhibition drew wide attention, and many people were moved by Lina’s paintings and filled with admiration and support for her dream. Most importantly, in all of this Lina found inner peace and joy.

This story tells us that when we keep pursuing our dreams, though we may meet difficulties and setbacks, God will give us a glory greater than before. He will use our talents and efforts to lead us toward a good future.

So whatever challenge or difficulty we face, let us remember God’s promise that He will surely give us peace. When we walk with God and trust His will, He will lead us beyond our own abilities and give us heavenly peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s glory and peace beyond imagination on your journey of pursuing your dreams. Amen!

v: Let them shout for joy, and be glad, who favor my righteous cause. Yes, let them say continually, “Yahweh be magnified, who has pleasure in the prosperity of his servant!”
